MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules take effect, restricting vague eco claims on wine labels
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, enforced from September 27, bans vague environmental claims such as 'eco-friendly' and 'clean' on consumer products, including wine.
Non-certified sustainability badges and unsubstantiated terms like 'natural' face stricter rules, with old stock not grandfathered and fines up to four percent of turnover.
Enforcement is left to individual member states, with the Sustainable Wine Roundtable's Peter Stanbury warning of divergent national frameworks across 27 countries.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded wine value as Burgundy's share jumps
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value on the Liv-ex fine-wine market, extending its lead.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanée-Conti and Domaine Leflaive top-traded by value.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6% led by Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: California table grape supply to last through December for holiday retail promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission says California grapes stay available in promotable volumes throughout December despite an early harvest.
Harvest is expected to end in mid-November, but shipments continue well beyond the last picking, supported by cold storage supplies.
Commission president Ian LeMay cites consumer research showing 72% of grape buyers prefer U.S.-grown grapes over imports, under 5% imports.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads Liv-ex trade with Lynch-Bages 2005 top-traded wine
MARKET.summ: US and UK buyers both upped their purchasing, the former segment reclaiming their share of purchasing
takeaways: Bordeaux led the Liv-ex fine wine market with a 37.4% share of purchases, with Lynch-Bages 2005 the top-traded wine.
Burgundy's share fell to 15.4% from 18.4% the previous week, below a September average of 24.6%.
US buyers, mostly for California wines, lifted their share to 9.6% and took over half of Bordeaux's purchased value.

MARKET.head: Surrey funds 17 rural projects, including a vineyard bird-repelling laser
MARKET.summ: A wine producer using bird-repelling lasers and cattle farmer using GPS collars to track livestock are among 17 innovative projects funded from a £500,000 pot to boost Surrey’s rural economy. Surrey County Council’s Farming Innovation Accelerator supports farmers and growers with funding for projects to modernise operations,...
takeaways: Surrey County Council's Farming Innovation Accelerator is funding 17 rural and farming projects from a £500,000 pot.
Each of the 17 recipients receives a grant of up to £35,000 plus bespoke expert support, from over 50 proposals.
Albury Vineyard will install an automated bird-repellent laser across 18 acres of grapevines, expected to add 1,700+ bottles yearly.

CULTURE.head: Plumpton College offers Level 3 viticulture apprenticeship to UK vineyards
CULTURE.summ: Develop the skills your business needs, invest in emerging talent and help shape the future of the UK wine industry with a Viticulture Apprenticeship at Plumpton College. As the UK wine industry continues to grow, developing a skilled workforce is essential to its long-term success. Plumpton College’s Level 3 Viticulture...
takeaways: Plumpton College is recruiting its next Level 3 Viticulture Apprenticeship cohort, starting 9 November.
Government funds 100% of training costs for eligible non-levy-paying SMEs' apprentices aged 16 to 24.
The qualification is endorsed by WineGB and combines workplace experience with block weeks of college learning.

SCIENCE.head: Enartis argues oak alternatives should be chosen by winemaking objective, not cost
SCIENCE.summ: Oak remains one of the most powerful tools available to winemakers for shaping wine style, structure, and complexity. While traditional barrel ageing continues to play an important role, modern oak alternatives offer greater flexibility, lower cost, and increased precision when used with a clearly defined objective.
takeaways: Oak alternatives like INCANTO chips and powders are chosen by objective: aroma, colour stability, or mouthfeel.
Toast level shapes aroma: light toast gives fresh oak and coconut, medium gives vanilla and caramel, heavy gives smoke and cocoa.
Oak tannins help colour stability mainly when added during maturation with micro-oxygenation, not during active fermentation.

SCIENCE.head: England's 2026 vines hit by frosts, heatwaves and drought, with Bacchus worst affected
SCIENCE.summ: With harvest complete, or nearing completion on many vineyards, Hutchinsons agronomists Rob Saunders and Will Robinson look at the impact of the record-breaking summer and what we can learn for future seasons. While 2026 could be remembered as a vintage season for some growers, others will look back less fondly, having first...
takeaways: England's 2026 season saw May frosts, then repeated heatwaves and drought, with 54 Met Office stations breaking daily maximum records.
Harvest came 10-14 days earlier than normal, with Sauvignon Blanc performing strongly while Bacchus struggled with intense heat and UV.
Viticulturist Markus Keller says photosynthesis suffers above 30°C, and leaves at 40-45°C can suffer irreparable damage.

SCIENCE.head: UK vineyards navigate early, hot, dry 2026 harvest after frost
SCIENCE.summ: After a run of dramatically different vintages, 2026 has given UK viticulture another season that challenged assumptions, but also demonstrated just how much English and Welsh vineyards can achieve. The 2026 growing season began with a series of extraordinary frost events, creating a challenging start before developing into a...
takeaways: The 2026 English and Welsh growing season began with severe frost, then turned warm and dry with rapid ripening.
Harvest started several weeks early at some vineyards, with dry weather keeping disease pressure low and fruit healthy.
Growers say heat, drought and early ripening now matter more, pushing adaptation through soil health and canopy management.

SCIENCE.head: Domaine Bousquet details its organic and water-saving practices in Mendoza
SCIENCE.summ: Domaine Bousquet continues to elevate Argentine wine through generations of dedication and innovation in organic wine practices. Earlier this year, Irma Remigio and her team warmly welcomed SWR’s Membership Manager, Ilva Fridenberga, to their winery. The winery, located at the foot of the Andes Mountains, is globally recognized...
takeaways: Sustainable Wine Roundtable membership manager Ilva Fridenberga visited Domaine Bousquet in Mendoza, Argentina, in February.
The estate is trialing biodiversity and garden corridors between vine rows, with harvest done from outside the rows.
It switched to high-pressure hoses for cleaning harvest boxes and is a signatory of the Bottle Weight Accord, targeting still-wine bottles under 420g.

SCIENCE.head: Portuguese trial cuts vine yields with Ethephon or hand thinning, varietal results differ
SCIENCE.summ: Some years, climate conditions and biological events increment the fertility of vines, which can lead to over cropping and a decrease of wine quality
takeaways: A 2007 Vinhos Verdes trial tested yield control on Loureiro (white) and Borraçal (red) vines using chemicals and manual thinning.
Ethephon and manual bunch thinning significantly reduced crop for both varieties, while Prohexadione-calcium had no significant effect on yield.
Manual thinning cut Borraçal yield about 41% versus control, and Loureiro about 26%, with quality gains only in Loureiro.

SCIENCE.head: Grenache rootstocks and irrigation shape water use and stomatal control in NE Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Under the context of global change, any decrease in water use by crops is essential, because water is becoming a more and more scarce resource, especially in Mediterranean areas, where grapevines are grown
takeaways: A 2007-2008 Spanish study at IRTA-Torre Marimon grew three-year-old Grenache on rootstocks 110-R, 41-B and 161-49C, irrigated or not.
Water use efficiency was higher in non-irrigated vines, and higher on 110-R and 41-B than on 161-49C.
In irrigated vines stomata stayed open despite low leaf water potential, suggesting hormonal signals outweigh hydraulic ones.

SCIENCE.head: Italian researchers outline viticulture strategies for climate change and biodiversity
SCIENCE.summ: In the globalization conditions possible future scenarios, optimistic and pessimistic are supposed
takeaways: Pisa University researchers argue climate change may extend viticulture to higher latitudes and altitudes, needing more resistant genotypes.
Several Italian regions launched a project to recover local grape varieties at risk of abandonment, such as Malvasia of Lazio and Cesanese d'Affile.
The paper reports viticultural and economic trials on Lazio varieties and Cabernet Sauvignon grown on the Cordon Spur of Conegliano system.

SCIENCE.head: Winter vineyard tools cut pruning labour and frost losses
SCIENCE.summ: As autumn turns to winter a list of jobs looms large in the calendar. The vines need pruning and the soil needs care and attention. To make these jobs less demanding and costly, different tools can be used.
takeaways: Zanon cordless battery-powered secateurs have grown popular for hand pruning, making winter pruning quicker and less arduous.
Provitis tractor-mounted pre-pruner cuts tendrils, reducing time spent pulling out canes after pruning.
Late spring frost protection options include candles, wind machines and the Ventigel, which combines heat and wind.

SCIENCE.head: Vine balance concept explained: crop load and growth dynamics across the season
SCIENCE.summ: Vine balance is a commonly used term in viticulture that expresses the concept of an appropriate balance of vegetative to reproductive growth of the vine
takeaways: Vine balance means proportioning vegetative growth to reproductive growth so the vine ripens its crop and sets next year's buds.
Common indirect measures such as yield to pruning weight ratio fail to capture how growth balances shift during the season.
A dynamic carbohydrate simulation model can show seasonal vegetative and reproductive demand against canopy carbon supply.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/1/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2026 Harvest Is In , Here’s What It’s Already Telling Us About this Burgundy Wine Vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Early harvest data from the 2026 Burgundy vintage reveals exciting insights into the region's grapes, offering a first look at vine yields and pricing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy's Côte d'Or picking finished 10–12 September, and the Comité des Vins de Bourgogne called the 2026 harvest its earliest ever recorded.
Early Comité estimates put Burgundy's 2026 crop around 30 per cent below the five-year average, with the official yield due mid-November.
The Comité described the fruit as healthy, with small berries, rich juice, and acidity that largely held up despite the heat.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Exploring the Roussillon (7) Château Nadal Hainaut
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Château Nadal Hainaut, an organic wine producer in the Roussillon making some nice wines. This visit was with Pauline Nadal,
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Château Nadal Hainaut in the Roussillon farms 27 hectares of vines, with 10 varieties, all organically.
Pauline Nadal, a sixth-generation family member and trained ceramicist, is responsible for production at the estate.
The estate's Signum 2020 Côtes du Roussillon, mainly Syrah, is rated 94/100, with 1800 bottles made.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Albarino? Soleri? Pinot Iskra? New White Wine Player in China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Attendees of the China Sommelier Summit in Shanghai were treated to a new local white wine producer pouring smack dab in the middle of the
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Lan Yue, established in Yantai in 2021, poured six wines at the China Sommelier Summit in Shanghai.
The winery planted its first vines in 2023 and recently released its first wines, with its Albarino singled out as notable.
Lan Yue's vineyards cover about 230 mu (15.5 hectares), including 40 mu (2.7 hectares) of Albarino, on Shandong's Penglai coast.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks going back this Sunday starts what she calls Kitchen Season.
During November and December, the author writes that people feel a special urge to cook for others.
Maker's article lists kitchen tools she uses year-round, which she says become even more essential during the festive season.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting Diaries: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Niagara’s Cabernet Franc harvest finally gets underway, plus the bottles that made my October memorable
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Buttonwood Grove's 2025 Blanc de Franc from Finger Lakes' Cayuga Lake is a white Cabernet Franc, listed at $24 USD.
Château de Fosse Sèche's 2018 Éolithe VDF from Saumur is praised for freshness and restraint in a warm vintage, with 5+ years of life ahead.
Fogolar Wines' 2018 Cabernet Franc "Picone Vineyard" from Ontario's Vinemount Ridge is described as cellar-worthy, from some of Ontario's oldest vines planted in the early 1980s.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A New White Zin
NEWSLETTERS.summ: If you are not familiar with the lore of White Zinfandel , America’s greatest contribution to wine culture , you are missing out on some excellent cocktail conversation. I understand this might sound like the layup for a bad wine joke, but I’m not being facetious. White Zinfandel is as important to the United States
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues the US wine industry is due a new White Zinfandel-style category, which he proposes calling "Relevé.".
Atkin describes Relevé as a field blend of red and white grapes from an entire estate or region, inspired by The Feudal Project's Mrs. Crabtree's field blend.
Atkin says the US drank 49.2 million bottles of White Zinfandel in 2024, despite wine sales being at an all-time low.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near Pontevedra, Galicia, ages magnums of its Albariño underwater in the O Grove estuary.
The Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months underwater at 13-16C and is made from the same wine as the 120,000-bottle 'Standard' version.
Glass caps replace cork on the underwater bottles because the family found cork unreliable despite waterproofing, according to Laura Vázquez.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Visiting the Vineyard in the Sky
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The extraordinary story of Domaine de Beudon in Valais, Switzerland
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Marion Granges-Faiss runs Domaine de Beudon in Valais, a six-hectare vineyard at 890 metres that the family has farmed for over 50 years.
Jacky Granges-Faiss bought Domaine de Beudon in 1971; he died in June 2016 when a caterpillar he was using reversed over him.
Domaine de Beudon became Valais's first Demeter-certified estate in 1992, and its wines are bottled unfiltered with sulphites as the only additive since 2003.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude published reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the 2024 Port vintage.
The author follows those posts with another covering older vintage Port selections tasted at the same event.
The older selections span vintages from 1985 to 2022, per the title.
